questions.prompt: Tell me about a day when you went to a park or the countryside with your family or friends.

segments.text: Last summer I went to a park with my family for my brother's birthday.
We took a big basket with sandwiches, fruit and a cake, and we sat on a blanket under a tree. My brother and my cousins played football for hours.
At the end, we all sang happy birthday and ate the cake in the sun. It was a lovely afternoon.
The day that comes to mind is a picnic we had last summer in the park to celebrate my brother's birthday.
We spread a blanket under a big tree and unpacked far too much food, while my brother and my cousins kicked a ball around for hours.
When the sun began to go down, we sang to him and shared out the cake, and nobody wanted to go home.

questions.prompt: How did you feel about that day?

segments.text: I felt very happy that day.
It was the first time all my family was together in months, so it was special. I was also a bit nervous at the start because I had to organise all the games for the children.
When we went home I was tired, but I felt grateful for such a good day.
Honestly, I felt completely happy, and a little proud as well.
It was the first time in months that the whole family had been together, so it felt special, although I was slightly nervous at the start because I had organised all the games.
By the evening I was exhausted, but I remember thinking how lucky I was to have such a close family.

questions.prompt: Do you think it is better to spend free time outdoors or at home? Why?

segments.text: I think it is better to spend free time outdoors, but not always.
When you are outside, you get fresh air and exercise, and you can meet people. After a week at the office, it is good to see something different.
However, on cold or rainy days I prefer to stay at home with a film and a hot drink.
On balance, I'd say outdoors, although it depends on the weather and on how tired I am.
Fresh air and a bit of exercise do wonders for your mood, and being outside is a great way to meet people, especially after a long week stuck indoors at a desk.
Then again, I wouldn't say no to a quiet evening at home with a good film if it were pouring with rain.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time when you cooked a meal for other people.

segments.text: A few months ago I cooked dinner for my friends at my flat.
My friend Laura helped me in the kitchen. She chopped the vegetables and I stirred a big pot of chicken soup. We made a salad and a chocolate cake too, because I wanted a real party.
Six people came, and everybody ate a lot. We talked until midnight.
I cooked dinner for six friends at my flat a few months ago, and I was determined to impress them.
My friend Laura helped by chopping the vegetables while I stirred an enormous pot of chicken soup, and between us we also managed to make a salad and a chocolate cake.
Everybody ate far more than I expected, and we sat around the table talking until midnight.

questions.prompt: How did you feel about it?

segments.text: I was quite nervous before the dinner.
I had never cooked for so many people, and I was afraid the soup would be too salty. I checked the recipe three times, and I couldn't sit down until everybody was at the table.
In the end, everybody loved the food, and I felt very proud and relieved.

questions.prompt: Do you think it is better to cook at home or to eat in restaurants? Why?

segments.text: I think it is better to cook at home most of the time.
It is cheaper and healthier, because you know exactly what is in your food. Also, cooking with other people is fun and you can learn new recipes.
But I like going to a restaurant on special days, because nobody has to wash the dishes!
On the whole, I'd say cooking at home wins, as long as you have the time.
It works out cheaper and healthier because you control what goes into your food, and cooking with other people is a good way to pick up new recipes and to catch up with them.
Mind you, for a birthday or a special occasion, nothing beats a restaurant, if only because someone else does the washing-up.
